## Tours featuring Floreana Island in the Galápagos

[Floreana](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) is one of the inhabited [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), where marine wildlife meets the history of settlement and seafaring. Its attractions include Post Office Bay with its traditional mail barrel and Punta Cormorant, whose lagoon provides opportunities to observe flamingos. The island itinerary depends on authorized landing sites and the vessel's schedule.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Floreana on the main route. These are two distinct formats: an eight-day cruise around the archipelago and a longer journey ending with the Galápagos after exploring mainland Ecuador.

## Eight-day VIP Galápagos yacht cruise

The [8-day VIP Galápagos yacht cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/) takes place aboard the superyacht Aqua Mare. On Floreana, the itinerary includes a visit to the Punta Cormorant area, with its brackish lagoon and flamingos. The second part of the day includes Post Office Bay, where the old tradition of exchanging postcards survives.

This suits travelers wanting to devote most of their time to the islands, alternating landings, walks and wildlife watching. Consult the tour's own terms for the yacht, cabin arrangements and included services; the VIP designation does not replace these details. The order of visits depends on the voyage and authorized visiting schedule.

## Eighteen days including the Amazon, Andes and a marine cruise

The [18-day Ecuador and Galápagos cruise tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) begins with mainland Ecuador, including natural areas of the Amazon and Andes, before continuing to the Galápagos. The island section includes a four-day cruise aboard M/Y Grand Majestic, visiting Floreana and Española.

On this journey, Floreana is one stop on the marine segment. The program combines the historic postal bay and nature landings with other islands, including [Gardner Bay](/ecuador/place/gardner-bay/) on Española. This is attractive to travelers who want to compare Ecuador's ecosystems in one trip without spending the entire two weeks exclusively on the islands.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_galapagosskie_ostrova_na_vip_yakhte,tour_source_ekvador_zhivaya_priroda_s_kruizom_na_galapagosakh}}

## What makes Floreana special?

Around Punta Cormorant, the contrasts of island scenery are striking: dark volcanic areas, coastal sands of different shades, a brackish lagoon and seabirds. Flamingos may be present in shallow water, but their appearance cannot be guaranteed at a scheduled landing. Walks follow designated conservation trails with a guide.

At Post Office Bay, visitors continue a custom begun by whalers: leaving a postcard in the mail barrel and, if they wish, taking a message they can deliver personally. This brief experience gives Floreana a distinctive place among nature excursions. Inland sites connected with early settlers are also found on the island, but they are not included on every cruise.

## Choosing a format and preparing for your visit

If the Galápagos archipelago is your primary interest, consider the eight-day sea itinerary. If you want to see [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), the Amazon and the mountains first, compare the longer mainland-and-island journey. In either case, check the landing sites: the name Floreana alone does not guarantee a visit to all its bays.

For going ashore, bring light protective clothing, sunscreen and footwear suitable for sandy and rocky ground. Boat outings depend on wind and sea conditions. In the Galápagos, follow the licensed nature guide's instructions, stay at a distance from wildlife and remain on permitted trails.

## Frequently asked questions about Floreana tours

### Can I see flamingos on the island?

There is a lagoon near Punta Cormorant where flamingos occur. Sightings are possible, but the number of birds and viewing distance are not known in advance.

### Is Post Office Bay included on every tour?

There is no universal rule. Post Office Bay is included on the [eight-day VIP cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/). Check the precise sailing itinerary for other ships and dates.

### Should I choose Floreana or Española?

Both reveal different aspects of the archipelago. Floreana offers natural lagoons and the history of its postal bay; [Gardner Bay](/ecuador/place/gardner-bay/) on Española is known for its white beach and sea lions. Some cruises visit both.

### Do I need a separate excursion from the mainland?

Cruise itineraries involve a flight from mainland Ecuador to the archipelago, followed by sea passages between islands. Floreana is not an ordinary road excursion from Quito.

## Galápagos Islands: how to choose the islands and your travel itinerary

The Galápagos Islands lie in the Pacific Ocean approximately 1,000 kilometers from mainland [Ecuador](/ecuador/). The archipelago's isolation, the volcanic origin of its islands and the convergence of ocean currents created conditions for extraordinary plant and animal life. Giant tortoises, marine iguanas, sea lions, Darwin's finches and Galápagos penguins live here. The archipelago has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1978; the marine component of the property was expanded in 2001.

Plan your trip to the Galápagos **around specific islands and authorized landing sites**. Viewpoints, beaches, walking trails, snorkeling waters and diving sites are distributed across different parts of the archipelago. Even travel within one island may take a substantial part of a day. Not every site is accessible without an organized excursion.

## Which islands to choose on your first visit

[Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) makes a convenient travel base. It is home to [Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/), while the [Santa Cruz Highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/) offer opportunities to observe giant tortoises in their natural habitat. The more humid interior of the island contrasts with its dry coastal landscapes.

[Bartolomé](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/) attracts visitors with volcanic scenery and views of the distinctive Pinnacle Rock. A visit may combine a climb to a panoramic viewpoint with time in an authorized marine area. Landing and swimming arrangements depend on the specific excursion.

[Isabela](/ecuador/place/isabela-island/) offers volcanic landscapes, a long coastline and visits to natural areas of the island. An itinerary featuring Isabela needs more time for inter-island transfers than a short trip based entirely on Santa Cruz. Its coastal areas and [Concha de Perla Bay](/ecuador/place/concha-de-perla/) are particularly appealing if they feature in the selected program.

[San Cristóbal](/ecuador/place/san-cristobal-island/) is another independent center for travelers, with its own beaches and marine wildlife. Adding this island broadens the trip's geography, but requires checking transport schedules and excursion availability.

All four places lie in the same island province, but a travel product is built around specific permitted sites, not a promise to "see all the Galápagos" in a few days.

## What wildlife might you encounter?

**Giant tortoises** are primarily associated with terrestrial ecosystems. Trips into the highlands are popular on Santa Cruz. **Marine iguanas** inhabit coastal areas; unlike land iguanas, they are adapted to feed in the sea. **Sea lions** rest on shores and may swim near boats, but their proximity is not permission to touch them.

Seabirds can be observed on various islands, while underwater excursions may reveal rays, fish and other marine animals. No particular species can be guaranteed at a predetermined hour: breeding seasons, ocean conditions and natural behavior matter more than visitor expectations. This is particularly true of rare underwater encounters.

In the Galápagos, **do not feed or touch wildlife, and maintain your distance**. National Park authorities emphasize staying on authorized routes and using approved tourism services. Taking shells, plants, sand or other natural objects from the islands is forbidden.

## Sea cruise or island hotel?

The two main ways to organize the trip differ in logistics.

| Format | Key difference |
|---|---|
| Island hotel | Return to the same base after excursions |
| Expedition vessel | Travel between sites according to the itinerary |
| Standalone diving day | Underwater sites and specific requirements |

Staying in an island hotel suits travelers wanting to combine sea excursions with walks and leisure in a town. Longer outings require travel to the port and a return journey. An expedition vessel lets guests visit different regions under an approved schedule, but landing sites and duration depend on the operator, vessel and permitted locations.

**Scuba diving and snorkeling are not the same service.** Diving with equipment requires suitable certification or a designated training format, a separate briefing and conditions appropriate to the dive. We offer a standalone [two-dive excursion](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/galapagos-two-dive-day/), which should be treated as a specific product rather than something included in every island tour.

## When to visit: seasons, water and wildlife

Travel to the Galápagos is possible throughout the year, but weather and sea conditions vary. **December to May** is generally warmer, often with brief showers; **June to November** brings cooler currents that can make the water noticeably colder and the sea rougher. These are general seasonal patterns, not forecasts for specific dates.

Consider what matters most when choosing a month: lengthy boat excursions, snorkeling, diving, walks on land or observing particular birds. Two travelers may choose different months for the same archipelago. For marine activities, check water temperatures, wetsuit requirements and the likelihood of cancellations due to weather.

Do not judge the season solely by air temperature: cold water, sun, wind and boat motion all affect comfort. Bring sun protection for land excursions and a windbreaker and dry bag for the boat.

## Arrival and visiting protected areas

The islands are generally reached by air from mainland Ecuador, with flights arriving at Baltra or San Cristóbal, among other locations. A special entry-control regime applies to tourists visiting the province. The Galápagos Governing Council describes the **Tarjeta de Control de Tránsito (TCT)** and a preregistration process. Check rules, fees and required documents before traveling, taking your nationality and itinerary into account; this summary does not replace current official requirements.

Separate from transportation, National Park and marine reserve regulations apply. Park management determines permitted locations and activities, whether walking, snorkeling, kayaking, boat excursions or diving. Organized visits to protected areas must follow the rules on authorized guides and permits for the activities selected. An urban beach and a remote protected island may have very different visiting conditions.

Biosecurity controls also help prevent non-native species from reaching the islands. Pay particular attention to baggage, foodstuffs and other items you transport.

## The Galápagos on Ada Tours itineraries

If you want to combine the islands with the mainland Andes, compare how many actual days each trip spends in the Galápagos.

Our [8-day Entire Ecuador and Galápagos Islands tour](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-galapagos-islands/) explores mainland Quito, Mindo and Quilotoa before flying to the islands. The itinerary includes Baltra and Santa Cruz, then Bartolomé and **one of two alternatives: North Seymour or South Plaza**. This is a choice within the program, not a simultaneous visit to both islands.

The [14-day Ecuador and Galápagos Nature Discovery tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-nature-discovery/) devotes more time to the mainland, including the waterfalls of [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/) and the Mashpi cloud forest. To combine different countries, consider the [18-day Peru and Ecuador itinerary including the Galápagos](/multi-country/tour/peru-ecuador-galapagos-luxury-18-days/).

Compare not only overall duration but also nights on the islands, permitted marine excursions, flight inclusions, alternative island choices and the actual services included. Specific costs and restrictions are set out in each offer.

## Frequently asked questions about the Galápagos

### How are the Galápagos different from mainland Ecuador?

The main differences are their isolated island ecosystems, many endemic species and special conservation regime. On the mainland, travelers explore the Andes, cities and humid forests. In the Galápagos, itineraries depend on the specific islands and authorized marine sites.

### Can I see giant tortoises without a multi-day cruise?

Yes. On [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), for example, highland routes provide opportunities to see tortoises. Check the daily program of the specific tour to confirm such a visit.

### Do I need a guide for National Park walks?

Organized visits to protected areas follow the National Park rules, including authorized guide requirements. Arrangements vary by site, so check which excursion and guide are necessary.

### Can I combine the Galápagos and Peru?

Yes. Our catalog includes an [18-day Peru and Ecuador journey](/multi-country/tour/peru-ecuador-galapagos-luxury-18-days/). It requires planning flights and island time separately from visits to Peru's attractions.

## Galápagos Islands tours: choosing the right format

The [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) are Ecuador's Pacific archipelago, famous for giant tortoises, sea lions, marine iguanas and diverse birdlife. The islands vary greatly in their landscapes and permitted excursion routes. Thus, a "Galápagos tour" may mean a trip with day excursions from an island hotel, a yacht cruise or a multi-day mainland journey followed by a shorter island extension.

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with the archipelago on the main itinerary. To select a suitable program, compare **the number of island days, landing sites and accommodation format**, as well as domestic flights, fees and marine excursions included.

## Island visits combined with mainland Ecuador

[Entire Ecuador and Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-galapagos-islands/) lasts 8 days, combining the capital, the equator, Mindo cloud forest, [Quilotoa Lake](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/) and the islands. It provides a compact introduction to the country's very different natural regions.

[Ecuador in 9 Days: Quito, Cotopaxi, Mashpi and the Galápagos](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-quito-cotopaxi-mashpi-galapagos-9-days/) emphasizes the transition from the Andes and cloud forests to island wildlife. [Ecuador and Galápagos in 17 Days](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-adventure-17-days/) adds more active mainland stages. Consider their physical demands: rainforest walks and high-altitude trekking near volcanoes are different kinds of activity.

For travelers interested in cultural routes and nature across countries, there is an [18-day Peru and Ecuador journey](/multi-country/tour/peru-ecuador-galapagos-luxury-18-days/) and other multi-country programs. They offer a broad view of South America but usually allocate less time to each particular island than a cruise devoted to the archipelago.

## Cruise or excursions from a hotel?

A cruise itinerary allows passengers to move between islands while resting aboard the vessel and to visit approved sites on a set schedule. On the [18-day tour with a cruise](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/), the island portion includes a marine journey with landings on [Floreana](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) and [Española, including Gardner Bay](/ecuador/place/gardner-bay/).

Hotel-based programs follow another pattern: accommodation is on an inhabited island, with boat outings operating on separate schedules. On an [Ecuador trip combining Quito and the Galápagos](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-quito-galapagos-islands/), read the daily itinerary carefully rather than assuming that every distant island is included.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_ves_ekvador_i_galapagosskie_ostrova,tour_source_ekvador_krasota_i_priroda,tour_source_ekvador_aktivnyj_tur_s_galapagossom,tour_source_lyuksovyj_tur_v_peru_i_ehkvador_s_galapagosami_na_18_dnej}}

## Diving and wildlife watching

Beach walks, snorkeling and scuba diving are distinct activities. The archipelago is home to sea lions, sharks, turtles and many birds, but the wildlife differs by island, season and ocean conditions. No itinerary guarantees a close encounter with a wild animal.

If diving is your main interest, see the dedicated [4- or 5-day Galápagos diving tour](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/) and the [Diving](/interests/diving/) theme. Qualifications, eligibility and precise dive sites must be set out in a specialized program. A sightseeing tour around the islands may not include diving at all.

For observing terrestrial wildlife, explore [Nature and Wildlife](/interests/wildlife/). [Floreana](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) is known for birds and historic sites, while [Gardner Bay](/ecuador/place/gardner-bay/) is famous for sea lion colonies on the beach. Check the islands visited before choosing a tour to see a particular species.

## Planning a journey to the archipelago

Travelers generally fly to the Galápagos from mainland Ecuador. Subsequent logistics depend on the arrival island, booked vessel and authorized itinerary. Domestic flights, compulsory fees, transfers and personal expenses may be additional to the base tour price. Their inclusion varies, so consult current official documents and the specific tour offer.

Protected parts of the National Park are visited under established rules with authorized guides and on marked trails. Keep your distance from animals, do not feed them and do not bring food or plants to the islands that might disturb local ecosystems. Ada Tours helps coordinate the island program with domestic flights and the rest of the Ecuador journey.

## Frequently asked questions about Galápagos tours

### How many days should I spend on the islands?

A short island segment can work for a first introduction, but several distant islands require more time. Count **days actually spent in the archipelago**, not the total length of the Ecuador tour.

### Can I see giant tortoises on every tour?

No. It depends on the exact land itinerary. If tortoise observation is your main goal, choose a program with the relevant protected area, rather than a general mention of the archipelago.

### Which is better: yacht or hotel?

A yacht makes successive landings on several islands more convenient; a hotel provides one base with separate excursions. Compare the actual stops, sea passages and comfort requirements, including your tolerance of boat motion.

### Are there tours combining the Galápagos and Peru?

Yes. For example, the [18-day Peru and Ecuador itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-ecuador-galapagos-luxury-18-days/) combines an island segment with mainland attractions. Check the daily contents individually.

## Gardner Bay: a white beach and sea lions in the Galápagos

Gardner Bay is located on [Española Island](/ecuador/place/espanola-island/) in the [Galápagos archipelago](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). This stretch of coastline is famous for its broad strip of pale coral sand and colonies of Galápagos sea lions.

Unlike many volcanic shores in the archipelago, the first impression here comes from the sandy beach. Sea lions lie at the water's edge, move across the sand and sometimes swim near shore. They can be watched during an unhurried walk, provided visitors maintain the necessary distance.

Española is one of the oldest Galápagos islands. Distinctive animals evolved here, including the Española mockingbird and other endemic species. Around the bay, you may see how these birds behave close to the shoreline and resting sea lions.

## Watching sea lions safely on the beach

Galápagos sea lions may seem accustomed to the presence of people, but they are wild animals. Their behavior can change, particularly near pups or during disputes between males.

The main rule is **do not approach too closely**, attempt to pet or feed them, or stand between a sea lion and the water. While walking along the beach, ensure that animals have an unobstructed path.

Sea lions often fill the foreground of photographs taken at Gardner Bay. But plan a trip around the opportunity for peaceful observation, rather than a promise of a specific number of animals in a photograph. Weather and season affect the colony's behavior.

## Española mockingbirds and other birds

The Española mockingbird is one of the island's characteristic birds. It may show considerable curiosity about visitors. Feeding birds, even inadvertently, disrupts their natural behavior and is prohibited under National Park rules.

Other marine and land birds live near the coast. Crabs can be observed on rocky stretches and, when conditions allow, marine iguanas. Light binoculars help you see details without approaching wildlife.

Española is also famous for breeding waved albatrosses, but their main nesting areas are not directly on Gardner Bay's sandy beach. Other sites on the island offer opportunities to observe them; inclusion of Gardner Bay does not itself mean a visit to an albatross colony.

## Snorkeling and the waters near the bay

Snorkeling may be available near Gardner Bay. Operators usually select permitted sites near rocks or neighboring islets where fish, rays and sometimes sea turtles and sea lions can be observed in the water.

| Format | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Beach walk | Sea lions and birds |
| Boat observation | Española coastline |
| Snorkeling | Marine life at authorized sites |

Snorkeling is possible only when currents and waves allow, and its inclusion should be confirmed in advance. Even a seemingly calm bay may have areas where entering the water is restricted. The guide identifies safe entry and exit points and provides instructions.

Snorkeling should be distinguished from scuba diving. They are separate activities with different preparation and supervision requirements. Do not expect a scuba diving excursion simply because the island's underwater life is described.

## How to reach Gardner Bay

Española is in the southern Galápagos archipelago. Gardner Bay is generally visited as part of a marine cruise, with travelers transferred to the beach from an expedition vessel in smaller boats. The landing may be wet, so prepare shoes and hand luggage for contact with water.

The island's visitor sites differ. Gardner is known for its sandy shore and sea lions, while other routes explore rocky cliffs, seabirds and different coastal landscapes. One bay does not replace the full Española program.

The [18-day Ada Tours Ecuador and Galápagos journey](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) includes Española in its marine portion. Check the exact island sequence and stop format: a long trip may combine beach wildlife observation, walks and snorkeling at different locations.

## When to go and what to bring

The Galápagos have warmer and cooler periods affecting water temperature and sea conditions. Sea lions and birds can nevertheless be observed at different times of year. When choosing a journey, the overall island itinerary and time allocated to each landing are more important.

On the beach, bring sun protection, drinking water, a hat, light clothing and footwear suitable for getting off a small boat. If snorkeling is planned, check whether a mask, fins, wetsuit and safety equipment are provided.

National Park rules require keeping enough space between visitors and wildlife. Collecting sand or shells, feeding birds or sea lions and leaving permitted areas are prohibited.

## Frequently asked questions about Gardner Bay

### Where is Gardner Bay?

On Española Island in the southern Galápagos archipelago of Ecuador.

### Can I watch sea lions from the shore?

Yes. The bay is known for sea lion colonies resting on the sand, although conditions and animal numbers vary from day to day.

### Is snorkeling possible at Gardner Bay?

It may be offered at authorized sites when weather is safe and the vessel's itinerary includes it.

### How does Gardner differ from other Española locations?

It is primarily a beach and wildlife stop. Other parts of the island are known for rocky trails and colonies of seabirds.

[Gardner Bay](/ecuador/place/gardner-bay/) lies on Española Island in the [Galápagos archipelago](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). A white beach slopes toward clear water, while sea lions rest on the sand. It is a wonderful place to observe wildlife calmly: animals move freely between shore and ocean.

## An eighteen-day itinerary visiting Española

The [18-day Ecuador and Galápagos cruise tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) combines the Amazon, highlands and mainland cloud forests with a four-day marine section aboard M/Y Grand Majestic. After arriving in the archipelago, travelers visit authorized natural sites on several islands.

One day is spent on Española, combining Punta Suárez and Gardner Bay. After the first excursion, the vessel approaches the bay, where a beach inhabited by sea lions awaits. The sequence lets visitors experience different kinds of coastline on the same island in one day.

## What is Gardner Bay like?

A wide stretch of pale sand, turquoise water and sea lion colonies make the bay recognizable. Observe the animals from a safe distance, leaving them room to reach the water. National Park rules prohibit touching or feeding wild animals.

Mockingbirds and other Galápagos birds can be found along the shore. Depending on the itinerary and sea conditions, snorkeling near coastal rocks may be available. Simply stopping at the bay, however, does not guarantee swimming or diving: permitted activities and the guide's decisions depend on the actual sailing.

## Gardner Bay and the cruise's other stops

Española offers several very different natural sites. Punta Suárez is known for rocky coastline and birds, while Gardner Bay is better suited to observing sea lions at the water's edge. On a cruise, consider both stops and their sequence.

The same longer tour also includes [Floreana](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/), with Post Office Bay and other nature sites. Floreana and Española offer different experiences: one has a strong seafaring-history element, while the other features beaches and wildlife. The separate [Galápagos tours catalog](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/tour/) lets you compare a broader selection of itineraries.

## Landing arrangements and wildlife rules

Sea approaches, weather and conservation restrictions affect the exact day and order of landings. National Park excursions follow designated routes with an authorized guide. Visitors should keep a distance of at least approximately 2 m from animals, remain in permitted areas and take all rubbish away.

Bring sun protection, water and belongings easy to carry when landing from a small boat. If snorkeling is planned, check whether it is possible and included on the particular cruise. Ada Tours helps coordinate the island portion with flights and the rest of the Ecuador itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about Gardner Bay

### Where is Gardner Bay?

On Española Island in Ecuador's Galápagos archipelago. This is not a beach near mainland [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) and cannot be reached by road.

### Can I see sea lions?

The bay is known for its sea lion colony. The animals move freely, however, and the exact number present at any particular landing is unknown.

### Is Gardner Bay included on all Galápagos cruises?

No. Visiting depends on the route approved for the particular vessel. The bay is included in the [18-day tour with a cruise](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/).

### Is this a standalone beach resort?

The bay is inside the protected National Park, and visits follow its rules. Its main purpose is wildlife observation, not a conventional resort stay.
